ticket_id: CW-17 (C-D63 host shell restart + confirmed force-kill)
criteria: existing OMP restart pattern (C-D62): Backend.restart_pane / _respawn in src/workbench/backend/service.py, ui_v1 RESTART_PANE and reasons, state push after ok in ui_server.py
required_behavior: First read how the backend owns the host shell (PersistentShell, shell selection Bash->sh, rcfile/hooks incl. wb-handoff, cwd, PTY, pidfd/session pinning from the P2-2 design, input owner user/manager, control modes, held handoff, takeover state, manager in-flight shell commands, records) and how its exit is detected today.

Restart: extend restart_pane to host_shell. Accept only when the host shell has exited (reaped). Start a new persistent shell exactly like at backend start (same shell selection, rcfile/hooks, env, cwd = the start cwd), new pane session_id/generation, input owner = user, control mode/handoff/takeover state reset to the fresh-start state, any manager in-flight shell command or pending result is closed as failed/unknown (never success) with a reason, phase recomputed (ready when everything else is healthy), state pushed to UIs, restart history recorded. Same refusals as OMP restart (pane_alive, restart_in_progress, restart_failed).

Force-kill: new ui_v1 client request kill_pane with pane field; only host_shell is accepted (OMP panes refused with a reason; OMP exit stays via the OMP itself). The UI performs the two-step confirmation; the backend executes immediately on the request. Terminate the host shell and every process in its session/process groups/jobs (escalate SIGHUP/SIGTERM -> SIGKILL with a bounded wait, using the pinned identities so no recycled PID is signalled); processes that setsid'd away are not targeted. Allowed whatever the input owner is; the result reports whether the manager owned the shell and whether a manager command was in flight. Afterwards the pane is exited (UI then offers Enter restart). Never touch OMP panes or the backend. Refuse during shutdown.
Snapshot exposes for host_shell: alive, exit_status, and enough to let the UI warn (input owner, manager command in flight).
acceptance: red->green tests: tests/contracts/test_ui_v1.py (kill_pane parse; restart_pane host_shell), tests/backend (ui_server dispatch, service-level kill and restart with the real PersistentShell in a temp dir: child jobs and background jobs die, a setsid daemon survives and is reported/left, owner/mode reset, manager in-flight command closed not-success, refusals, concurrent requests, repeated kill/restart cycles without fd/process leaks)
list *_independent* tests that fail because they enumerate the contract or assume the old host-shell rules (do not edit them)
run tests/backend, tests/contracts, tests/ui (pattern test_*.py, no pipe, real exit code), tests/gates (g1_vt with PYTHONPATH=src:.)

live: backend in a temp data dir with the real shell (no model prompt), run a long job and a background job in the host shell, kill_pane via ui_v1, verify they are gone, restart_pane host_shell, verify a fresh prompt, wb-handoff available, owner user; clean up everything you started
